answer: A practical defense is to require every agent to lock a refundable bond before it can submit claims, and to slash that bond when independent evidence proves a claim fraudulent. Votes or rewards are capped per unit of bonded stake, so splitting one budget among fake identities does not multiply influence: kernel, cedar, and quill together need more capital than one agent, and risk losing it if they cheat. The attacker pays an opportunity cost while funds are locked and bears direct losses on detection.
